key_insight: Denoising diffusion models generate realistic additive-manufacturing orientation micrographs and support inverse mappings from properties or processes to microstructure.
engineering_relevance: Synthetic microstructures could strengthen digital-twin workflows and help accelerate additive-manufacturing materials qualification.
method: Train denoising diffusion probabilistic models to synthesize orientation-imaging micrographs.
Use classifier-free guidance for property-to-structure and process-to-structure inverse problems.
Demonstrate a qualification-relevant uncertainty quantification application.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative evidence of generated-sample fidelity but provides no dataset sizes, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
watch_item: Micrograph fidelity alone does not establish accurate downstream mechanical predictions; validation across relevant manufacturing conditions remains important.
paper_title: Microstructural Generative Inverse Models for Additive Manufacturing Digital Twins
